=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/internal-cancel-on-pr-close.yml: lines 44-49 (Checkout main step); cross-reference tests/test_review_merge_train.py:490 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The new heal-pr-reconcile job contains a step "Checkout main" with uses: actions/checkout@v5 (line 45). The contract test test_cancel_on_close_wrappers_keep_event_and_add_matching_schedule at tests/test_review_merge_train.py:490 asserts assert "checkout" not in workflow.lower() for both internal-cancel-on-pr-close.yml and workflow-templates/ai-cancel-on-pr-close.yml. CI run 35991067344 already failed this test on the PR head SHA 1af233beadae71be275a527fb976d8c9cbcb8f3e ("assert 'checkout' not in 'name: \"inte...concile.sh\\n'" — "'checkout' is contained here: - name: checkout main").
  WHY: GitHub Actions will reject the PR merge because the CI lint step fails. The cancel-on-pr-close contract intentionally forbids the wrapper from checking out code (the wrapper's declared permissions are actions: write / contents: read / pull-requests: read and it should only cancel runs); the new job breaks that invariant. The PR added an exception to tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py for the integration-ref allowlist but did not touch the cancel-on-pr-close contract test, so the contract test still fires.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: lines 695-702 (_self_named_script fallback in extract_crash_file); regex _SELF_NAMED_SCRIPT_LINE_RE at line 1064 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The third fallback in extract_crash_file matches any line shaped <name>: <rest> where <name> is a script that exists in scripts/, regardless of whether the line is an error. The regex `^(?:::error::|##\[error\])?\s*(?P<name>[a-z][a-z0-9]*_[a-z0-9_]*(?:\.(?:sh|py))?): (?P<rest>\S.*)$` makes the `::error::` / `##[error]` prefix OPTIONAL, so a benign debug log line such as `gh_helpers: retry exhausted` or `write_opencode_config.sh: loaded 14 models` will be returned as scripts/gh_helpers.sh / scripts/write_opencode_config.sh even though no crash occurred in that file. The new tests test_extract_crash_file_on_self_named_script_errors codify this behavior, so the regression is intentional, but the function is also called from build_autofix_failure_payload at line 596 and its result feeds the ownership classifier classify_crash_ownership at line 723 — that output drives the pr-self-inflicted / base-self-inflicted / workflow-defect routing in the intake. A non-error line naming any scripts/<real>.sh will silently win over the higher-precision ::error:: patterns (which still run first, so the regression only fires when those miss — exactly the failure-evidence tail scenario the script is meant to handle).
  WHY: When the bounded failure_evidence tail lacks a `::error::` line and the shell `scripts/<name>: line N:` pattern, but contains an unrelated debug line that happens to look like `<script_name>: <rest>`, extract_crash_file returns the wrong crash file. The intake then classifies the heal as self-inflicted on a file the PR or its base did not actually break, and either files a wrong-target heal issue or skips the self-inflicted routing that would have caught a real defect.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_pr_reconcile.sh: _retarget_heal function lines 146-221, RETARGET_FAIL_REASON assignments | severity=high | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: When the merged-source path completes both merge steps and produces a non-empty diff against the base, the script pushes merged_sha with git push (line 205), then attempts to PATCH the heal PR's base ref (line 211-214) only when [ "${heal_base}" != "${BASE_REF}" ]. If the heal PR was already re-pointed to BASE_REF by GitHub when it auto-retargeted after the source PR merged, the push succeeds but no PATCH is attempted, so the script never confirms whether GitHub accepts the fast-forward push to a deleted source-branch ref. The PR's diff is only the heal changes if and only if the push was non-fast-forward-only-allowed; if the ruleset still rejects a non-ancestor push to a branch whose head SHA no longer exists, the script silently returns 0 and emits retargeted with a push that may not have landed.
  WHY: The fast-forward push to refs/heads/<heal_branch> requires the ruleset's allow-listed actors (or no non_fast_forward rule). If the repo has tightened rulesets since the last heal PR was filed, the push at line 205 will silently fail — git push returns non-zero, the `if !` branch at line 205-209 sets RETARGET_FAIL_REASON=push_rejected, and the calling code at line 249 logs skip reason=push_rejected instead of closing the heal PR. The heal PR is then left alive with its original (now-superseded) head, and no operator alert fires (the log line is warn-level only at line 250). The script's own docs claim "A merge conflict, nothing left to apply, or a missing base closes the heal PR and issue instead", but push_rejected is treated as a transient skip — exactly the silent-stranding scenario the script is supposed to prevent.
- .github/workflows/internal-cancel-on-pr-close.yml: lines 19-53 (heal-pr-reconcile job) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The cancel-on-pr-close wrapper's declared permissions are actions: write / contents: read / pull-requests: read at workflow scope (lines 9-13). The new heal-pr-reconcile job inherits those and adds actions/checkout@v5 with token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }} (line 48) to run a bash script that performs git fetch, git merge, git push, and writes back to refs/heads/<heal_branch> in the same repository. The cancel-on-pr-close wrapper contract (pinned by tests/test_review_merge_train.py:490 and by the agents.md "Internal-cancel-on-pr-close" allowlist rationale) explicitly limits the wrapper to cancel/cleanup; the new job expands effective state scope (git writes to branches other than its own ephemeral worktree) and effective capability scope (GH_PAT can rewrite branches, not just cancel runs). The kill switch WORKFLOW_HEAL_PR_RECONCILE_ENABLED (line 42) is honored by the bash script but the workflow itself always runs the checkout step before the script, so the expanded capability is still in scope even when the script no-ops.
  WHY: The script's first call is git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree, but the checkout step has already fetched refs/pull/<n>/head and refs/heads/<heal_branch> into the runner before that check runs. A misconfigured gate, race, or external write between the checkout and the script's skip logics (e.g. set WORKFLOW_HEAL_PR_RECONCILE_ENABLED=false) leaves a fetched heal_branch + source_head already present in the runner worktree even when no push is performed. There is no documented kill switch on the checkout step itself.
